relations.evidence: To select data from a document or keyspace, your client must have necessary privileges on the document or keyspace. The required privilege depends on your [cluster access credential type](../../clusters/cluster-rbac.md#cluster-access-credential-types). | Basic | [Read](../../clusters/cluster-rbac.md#basic-access-credentials) |

notable_absence.finding: Like other SELECT-clause components in this batch (comma.md, selectclause.md, selectintro.md), the ORDER BY clause carries only the data-plane credential-type privilege gate, never a management-plane capella-role:* requirement - reinforcing the round-2 hypothesis that requiresCapellaRole is reserved for statements that alter cluster/security state, not read-only query clauses.

cross_component_finding: The prerequisites text ('your client must have necessary privileges on the document or keyspace') attributes the requirement to whatever keyspace the ORDER BY clause's containing SELECT references - the clause itself doesn't introduce a distinct privilege, it merely inherits the SELECT statement's Read/Query Read gate. This is the credential-type/privilege model holding up cleanly on a purely syntactic sub-clause, not just top-level statements.
